text: Alex: FYI — we had a short burst of GPU oom_kill alerts in us-west-2 around 02:10 UTC. Pager fired twice for the same flapping nodes. Looking for quick ideas to cut noise without hiding real incidents. Maria: ugh, I saw that. Looks like three nodes hit memory pressure within ~90s windows then recovered. Paging on each alert is noisy. Jamal: Can we group by node + region and add a short suppression window? e.g., don't page if the same node has an alert within X mins. Olivia: I worry about hiding real rollouts that cause sustained failures. Maybe differentiate short bursts from sustained errors: burst = >=3 alerts in 2m that recover, sustained = >5m continuous error rate. Devon: Suggestion: keep page for sustained, ticket for short/isolated. We can implement a "burst window" policy in Alertmanager routes. Example route snippet: ```yaml route: group_by: [alertname, cluster, node] group_wait: 30s group_interval: 1m repeat_interval: 4h routes: - match: severity: warning continue: true mute_time_intervals: ["burst-noise"] ``` sre-bot: Mute-time-intervals currently support calendar windows. For burst-style dampening we use relabel/grouping + inhibition rules. Maria: We could create an alert expression that triggers a high-severity if error_rate over 5m > 5% or sustained OOMs > 3m, otherwise set severity=info/warning which goes to a ticketing handle. Jamal: Example Prom rule to separate transient vs sustained: ```promql # transient flares: >3 events in 2m gpu_oom_events_total{region="us-west-2"} - gpu_oom_events_total{region="us-west-2"}[2m] > 3 # sustained: rate over 5m increase(gpu_oom_events_total[5m]) > 0 ``` Olivia: Also propose regional dampening for us-west-2 during known noisy maintenance windows (eg driver pushes). Set a higher page threshold there and notify via channel instead. Ryan: For cost impact: paging dev time is expensive. If we drop a single pager that gets called 10x/day and it's usually noise, monthly savings in dev-hours is significant. But we need quick rollback if we under-page. Devon: Ops playbook idea — add a short automated suppression that converts repeated identical node alerts into a single page and add a ticket for every occurrence. If suppressed count > 10 in 30m escalate to page. Keeps visibility and avoids repeated wakeups. Maria: Can we implement this with Alertmanager inhibition + a small lambda that counts suppression occurrences and bumps severity? Or use our existing runbook-runner to escalate? sre-bot: runbook-runner supports escalation webhooks. Could create a job: on suppression_count >= 10 within 30m -> send high-priority to oncallPD. Alex: Action items: - Jamal: prototype Prom rules for burst vs sustained and post to PR (due EOD) - Olivia: draft region-specific dampening proposal and list known maintenance windows (due 24h) - Devon: sketch Alertmanager route + inhibition config and a lightweight escalator lambda (due 48h) - Maria: verify runbook-runner escalation hook works with suppressed alerts (help from Ryan) Ryan: I'll help test the runbook integration and estimate on-call hour reductions for the next all-hands. Alex: Thanks. One more note — keep grouping keys minimal to avoid over-grouping. group_by [alertname, cluster, node] + labels for region should be enough. Olivia: Also include a dashboard metric: suppressed_pager_count and suppressed_to_page_ratio so we can monitor if we're hiding too much. Jamal: I'll include grafana panels in the PR. Alex: Great — let's iterate quickly. :thumbsup:
